value.body: A veterinarian diagnoses, treats and prevents disease in pets, livestock and poultry. Many run their own clinic for companion or farm animals; others work in state animal husbandry departments, dairy cooperatives, farms and animal health companies. A clinic day involves examinations, vaccinations, minor surgery, prescribing treatment and farm visits.

items.label: Registration
items.value: Veterinary Council of India or a State Veterinary Council

items.label: Common work
items.value: Vaccination, deworming, surgery, artificial insemination, herd health

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, then a BVSc & AH: 15% of seats are filled through the Veterinary Council of India's all-India quota using NEET-UG, and the rest through state counselling. After registering, many new vets work at an established clinic or in a government post before opening their own practice.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Clinical examination and diagnosis across species
Minor surgery and anaesthesia for animals
Advising owners and farmers on feeding and care
Running a clinic: records, medicines stock, billing

value.title: At a glance
items: Starting a clinic needs money for space, equipment and medicines.
Pet practice is concentrated in towns and cities; farm-animal practice is mostly rural.
Other routes include an MVSc specialisation or veterinary officer posts through state recruitment.
